stemMd: One nucleotide is inserted near the beginning of a protein-coding sequence, after the start codon. No second mutation occurs. What is the most likely immediate coding consequence?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Only the inserted nucleotide is translated as a whole amino acid.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The entire chromosome doubles in number.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The reading frame must remain unchanged.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The downstream codon reading frame changes.

explanationMd: A ribosome groups bases into triplets from the start site. Adding one base shifts downstream grouping and can introduce a premature stop; earlier codons remain unchanged.

distractorRationale.c: A one-base insertion is not a multiple of three.
distractorRationale.b: A local insertion does not duplicate chromosomes.
distractorRationale.a: Codons contain three bases, not one.
distractorRationale.d: Codons before the insertion are unaffected.
